name: Frida - Dynamic Instrumentation Toolkit
description: Frida injects a JavaScript engine into a running process (Android/iOS/desktop) to hook and rewrite functions at runtime. In mobile testing it bypasses root/jailbreak and SSL-pinning checks, dumps decrypted traffic and crypto keys, traces method calls, and manipulates app logic live - without repackaging the app.
notes:
=== SETUP ===
  pip install frida-tools
  # push + run frida-server on a rooted device/emulator (matching arch/version):
  adb push frida-server /data/local/tmp/ ; adb shell "/data/local/tmp/frida-server &"

=== ENUMERATE ===
  frida-ps -U            # processes on USB device
  frida-ps -Uai          # installed apps + identifiers

=== ATTACH / SPAWN ===
  frida -U -f <target> -l <file>      # spawn app with a script (-f = package id)
  frida -U <target>                   # attach to running app

=== COMMON SCRIPTS ===
  frida -U --codeshare pcipolloni/universal-android-ssl-pinning-bypass-with-frida -f <target>
  frida-trace -U -f <target> -j '*!*crypt*'      # trace crypto methods

=== HOOK EXAMPLE (ssl pinning / root) ===
  Java.perform(function(){
    var X = Java.use('javax.net.ssl.X509TrustManager');
    // override checkServerTrusted to no-op ...
  });

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  objection      # Frida-powered, no-code runtime toolkit
  apktool patch  # static pinning/root bypass
  xposed/LSPosed # framework-level hooking

examples.label: Spawn app with a hook script

recommended.note: objection wraps Frida for common bypasses without scripting.
apktool for a static pinning/root bypass alternative.
jadx to find the methods to hook.

defense.why_it_works: Frida rewrites function behavior in the running process, so purely client-side checks (root/jailbreak detection, SSL pinning, license gates) can be neutralized at runtime even if the binary is obfuscated.
defense.prerequisites: A rooted/jailbroken device or emulator (or a repackaged app with a Frida gadget) and the target app installed.
defense.impact: Bypass of client-side security controls, interception of decrypted traffic/keys, and live manipulation of app logic.
defense.detection: On-device RASP can detect Frida (frida-server ports 27042/27043, injected threads, known library names, ptrace); backend can see anomalies (pinning-bypassed clients on unexpected networks, emulator fingerprints) if attestation is used.
defense.artifacts: Frida artifacts on-device (gum-js-loop thread, /data/local/tmp/frida-server, TCP 27042), integrity-attestation failures server-side.
defense.prevention: Runtime application self-protection (RASP) with Frida/debugger/emulator detection; Play Integrity / DeviceCheck/App Attest with server-side enforcement; defense-in-depth so no single client check is decisive; TLS pinning plus server-side auth; obfuscation to slow hook discovery.
